system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: Use `{{KEY}}` placeholders in your prompt to inject values from the `promptArgs` option.
system_prompt_style.note: Sandcastle orchestrates external agent CLIs; it supplies a user-authored prompt file with {{KEY}} substitution and !`command` expansion, not a system prompt of its own.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: Use `` !`command` `` expressions in your prompt to pull in dynamic context. Each expression is replaced with the command's stdout before the prompt is sent to the agent.
env_context_strategy.note: Underlying agent (Claude Code etc.) navigates the repo; optional shell-expansion context injection is user-authored.

context_compaction.note: Context management is delegated to the wrapped agent CLI; README does not describe history handling.

observation_format.evidence_quote: Fires for each text chunk, tool call, and raw stdout line the agent produces.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: `exec` | Both | Run a command, optionally streaming stdout line-by-line via `options.onLine`
tool_call_format.note: Sandcastle's own execution interface is shell commands; the agent's internal tool-call format belongs to the wrapped CLI.

tool_count.evidence_quote: Sandcastle uses a flexible prompt system. You write the prompt, and the engine executes it — no opinions about workflow, task management, or context sources are imposed.
tool_count.note: Sandcastle exposes no tools to the model itself; tools come from the wrapped agent CLI.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: A TypeScript library for orchestrating AI coding agents in isolated sandboxes
edit_primitive.note: No edit tool in the harness; edits are made by the wrapped agent, results collected as git commits.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: a long-lived MCP server, etc. — inherits the agent's stdout pipe and keeps it open
protocol_standardization.note: MCP only mentioned as a child process of the wrapped agent; Sandcastle itself implements no protocol client/server.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: Maximum number of agent iterations to run before stopping. Default: 1
loop_primitives.note: Default maxIterations 1; multi-run implement-then-review and sandbox.exec("npm test") gating are shipped patterns; templates include sequential-reviewer and parallel-planner.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: `parallel-planner` | Plans parallelizable issues, executes on separate branches, then merges
planning_granularity.note: Planning exists only as a prompt-driven template workflow, no harness-stored plan object (planner templates use a <plan> output schema).

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: `parallel-planner` | Plans parallelizable issues, executes on separate branches, then merges
multi_agent_topology.note: A single run() invokes one agent; pipeline/parallel multi-agent workflows are reachable via templates and repeated run() calls in user code.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: Agent provider — required. Pass a model string to claudeCode().
delegation_mechanism.note: No delegation primitive; the user's script sequences separate run() calls.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: When set, replaces Sandcastle's default `--dangerously-skip-permissions` on AFK runs.
human_in_loop.note: Default AFK runs bypass permissions; interactive() sessions exist but are user-driven TUI, and permissionMode can re-enable the agent's own prompting.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: `sessionId` | string? | Agent session ID from the provider stream

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: no opinions about workflow, task management, or context sources are imposed
long_term_memory.note: Session JSONL capture is run-scoped resume state, not a memory store.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: Pass `resumeSession` to `run()` to continue a prior Claude Code, Codex, or Pi conversation inside a new sandbox

self_verification.evidence_quote: `sequential-reviewer` | Implements issues one by one, with a code review step after each
self_verification.note: Review steps are shipped templates (a second agent run reviews the changes); test execution is a documented user-written sandbox.exec("npm test") gate, not harness-enforced by default.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: Pass `maxRetries` to have Sandcastle handle the retry loop for you. Each retry resumes the same agent session and feeds back a token-efficient description of the error
retry_policy.note: maxRetries defaults to 0 (structured-output validation retries only); maxIterations defaults to 1.

rollback.evidence_quote: Sandcastle creates a temporary branch in a git worktree. The agent works on the temp branch, and changes are merged back to HEAD when done.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: String (or array of strings) the agent emits to end the iteration loop early. Default: "<promise>COMPLETE</promise>"
termination_condition.note: maxIterations caps the loop (default 1); idle/completion timeouts also end runs (see F3).

cost_controls.evidence_quote: `usage` | `IterationUsage`? | Token usage snapshot from the last assistant message
cost_controls.note: Token usage is reported but no budget/cap or routing is enforced by Sandcastle.

timeouts.evidence_quote: Idle timeout in seconds — resets whenever the agent produces output. Default: 600 (10 minutes)
timeouts.note: Per-step lifecycle timeouts (copyToWorktreeMs, gitSetupMs, per-hook 60 s) plus agent idle/completion timeouts.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: Sandcastle needs an isolated environment to run agents in. Built-in options:
execution_isolation.note: docker() is the documented default in quick start; podman(), vercel() microVMs, and noSandbox() (host) are also shipped.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: For bind-mount providers (like Docker), the worktree directory is bind-mounted into the container — the agent writes directly to the host filesystem through the mount
filesystem_access.note: Within the container the agent sees the mounted worktree plus any configured mounts, some readonly.

network_policy.evidence_quote: Optional: attach container to Docker network(s) — string or string[]
network_policy.note: No egress restriction by default; agent uses gh/network inside container.

permission_model.evidence_quote: When set, replaces Sandcastle's default `--dangerously-skip-permissions` on AFK runs.
permission_model.note: Opt-in permissionMode / Codex approvalsReviewer enable per-call or AI-mediated approval.

tracing.evidence_quote: Optional: forward the agent's output stream to your own observability system. Fires for each text chunk, tool call, and raw stdout line the agent produces.
tracing.note: Default logging writes a file under .sandcastle/logs/; session JSONL is captured per iteration.

replayability.evidence_quote: Before the sandbox starts, Sandcastle validates that the session file exists on the host and transfers it into the sandbox

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: A TypeScript library for orchestrating AI coding agents in isolated sandboxes
eval_hooks.note: No benchmark evaluation runner in the file tree; tests are vitest unit tests.

guardrails.evidence_quote: Any `` !`…` `` pattern that appears inside an argument value is treated as inert text — it won't be executed against the host shell.
guardrails.note: Prompt-injection mitigation on promptArgs; no action blocklist or output masking in the harness.

target_domain.evidence_quote: Orchestrate sandboxed coding agents in TypeScript with sandcastle.run()

model_agnostic.note: Agent-provider-agnostic rather than a direct LLM client.
